reproduction_target: Computational analysis of a deep mutational scanning (TF-MAPS) study of four human TF DNA-binding domains (HNF1A, FOXG1, FOXP1, plus comparisons): DiMSum v1.3.2 processing of Illumina reads into variant fitness scores for bacterial-one-hybrid (binding) and spectinomycin-sandwich (abundance) selections; IC50 fitting and score normalisation in R; AlphaFold3 structure prediction; rSASA / DNA-contact / distance calculations (PyMOL, DNAproDB, ChimeraX-1.5); LOESS binding-residual modelling and exponential allosteric-decay fitting in R; PASSer/FPocket allosteric pocket prediction; clinical variant classification and statistical tests in R. Wet-lab work (mutagenic library design and cloning, B1H and spectinomycin selections, sequencing library preparation and NovaSeq sequencing) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the Methods sections 'Sequencing data processing', 'Structural analysis', 'Binding-residuals', 'Allosteric decay', 'Pocket prediction', 'Clinical variant interpretation', 'Statistical tests'. The repository (https://github.com/lehner-lab/TF-MAPS) landing page and README were read as prose only: it contains four R scripts (fitting_loess.R, distance_decay.R, chimera_defattr_visualisation.R, abundance_ic50_mean_abundance_comparisons.R), a LICENSE and a README; no lockfile, no container, no tags/releases, no environment file. Steps whose code is one of those four scripts get code=2; steps performed with third-party CLI/GUI/web tools with no script in the repo get code=1 (reconstructable from prose). Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: DiMSum v1.3.2 processing of raw Illumina NovaSeq S2 PE250 reads into variant counts/fitness, with stated settings mutagenesisType = codon, fitnessMinInputCountAll = 10, vsearchMinQual = 20, fitnessDropoutPseudocount = 0
IC50 estimation from the spectinomycin tripartite-sandwich assay across 21 concentrations using the drc R package (repo script abundance_ic50_mean_abundance_comparisons.R)

Selection of three consecutive spectinomycin concentrations by 'optimal separation between synonymous and nonsense variants', unweighted averaging across biological replicates, and normalisation of abundance and binding scores to the mode of synonymous and nonsense variants
AlphaFold3 prediction of the four TF-DBD:motif complexes, used as the reference structures for all downstream structural analysis
rSASA computation with the PyMOL built-in function; core residues rSASA < 25%, DNA-contacting residues delta-rSASA > 1% (bound vs unbound), remainder surface
Direct TF-DNA contact analysis and visualisation with DNAproDB (base-specific contacts reported for six residues)
Euclidean minimum residue-to-DNA distance calculation with the ChimeraX-1.5 'contacts' function, default parameters, VDW overlap threshold < 0.4 A
Structural alignment of FOXG1 and FOXP1 DBD monomers with the ChimeraX-1.5 'Matchmaker' function using 'Chain pairing' and 'Best-aligning pair of chains' options
Pairwise sequence alignment with the BLASTP 'Blast 2 Sequences' tool
Secondary-structure annotation with SSDraw on the AlphaFold3-predicted structure, coloured by pLDDT confidence scores

LOESS regression of binding on abundance at non-DNA-contacting positions to derive binding-residuals: R loess(), span = 0.9, weights = inverse variance of binding scores, two anchor points (0,0) and (-1,-1) at weight 1e+04; per-position median absolute residuals excluding abundance < -0.8 (repo script fitting_loess.R)

Exponential allosteric-decay fit of absolute binding-residuals vs minimum residue-DNA distance using nlsLM from the minpack.lm R package, model y = a*exp(-b*x) + c with a = max|residual|, c = min|residual|, b = 0.5 initialisation (repo script distance_decay.R)

Allosteric pocket identification and druggability prediction with the PASSer web server ensemble model (FPocket-based druggability scores), one chain defined, AlphaFold3 structure with mutated regions and DNA uploaded; resulting pocket PDBs visualised in ChimeraX

Clinical variant functional and biophysical classification by explicit thresholds (neutral: |effect| <= 0.1 and BH FDR >= 0.05; LoF: binding < -0.1 and FDR < 0.05; GoF: binding > 0.1 and FDR < 0.05; abundance-affecting / interface / allosteric residual rules)

Statistical testing in R: one-sample t-tests per variant with BH FDR correction; one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank tests per position/residue group with Bonferroni (n < 30) or BH (n >= 30); Kruskal-Wallis tests with post hoc Dunn's tests
Generation of ChimeraX DEFATTR files for 3D visualisation of median variant effects (repo script chimera_defattr_visualisation.R), rendered in ChimeraX-1.5
Variant library design and preparation: NNK/NNS/NNH codon-randomised oligo pools (IDT), PCR incorporation, MORF-library-derived wild-type DBD amplification, motif oligos
Plasmid library preparation: cloning into pB1H2w2-zif268, pH3U3-zif268 (omega) and PTB182 backbones, T4/HiFi ligation, transformation and coverage estimation
DNA-binding selection: liquid-format bacterial one-hybrid (B1H) assay in USO hisB- pyrF- rpoZ- cells with 1 mM 3-AT, 24 h at 37 C, input/output pellet collection
Abundance selection: spectinomycin tripartite sandwich assay in NEB 5-alpha cells across 21 serial spectinomycin dilutions, three biological replicates over three consecutive concentrations
Sequencing library preparation (two-step indexing PCR, SPRI clean-ups) and Illumina NovaSeq S2 PE250 sequencing at the Wellcome Sanger DNA pipeline

headline.static_readiness: 0/16 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 4/16 (25%) RI at the stage-1 ceiling (C1 DiMSum, C7 ChimeraX contacts, C8 ChimeraX Matchmaker, C16 DEFATTR generation) - these are the only steps whose version axis reaches 1 via an exact prose pin (DiMSum v1.3.2, ChimeraX-1.5). The remaining 12 steps cap at NI because the R version and every R package (drc, minpack.lm, GGally, ggplot2, ggpubr, gplots, stringr, dplyr) are unpinned, and AlphaFold3 / PyMOL / DNAproDB / SSDraw / BLASTP / PASSer are unversioned web or GUI tools. Because the repository carries no lockfile, no container and no release tag, environment closure is absent, so under the Delta-2 reading no step can exceed version = 1 and therefore no step is R-star-eligible even with stage-2 code verification.
headline.coverage: 16 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus the GitHub README prose; 5 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. Both a Data Availability statement (ENA PRJEB97482) and a Code Availability statement (github.com/lehner-lab/TF-MAPS) are present; intermediate RData objects are additionally deposited at Zenodo record 17457956 (named in the README, not in the paper).

gaps.where: Software environment for all 16 computational steps (repository root; Methods)
gaps.missing: No lockfile, container, conda environment file, renv.lock, sessionInfo() dump or requirements list anywhere in the repository or paper. The README's 'System Requirements' section names R packages (GGally, ggplot2, ggpubr, gplots, stringr, dplyr) with no versions and does not state an R version; the Methods cite R only as 'R Foundation, Vienna, 2021'. Exact pins exist for exactly two tools (DiMSum v1.3.2, ChimeraX-1.5).
gaps.how_to_close: Add renv.lock or a conda-lock/pixi.lock plus a container image digest covering R, drc, minpack.lm and the plotting packages, and record the resolved R version; this is the single change that would move the four RI steps toward R-star eligibility.

gaps.where: C1 (DiMSum run), C3 (concentration selection and normalisation), C4 (AlphaFold3), C5 (PyMOL rSASA), C6 (DNAproDB), C9 (BLASTP), C10 (SSDraw), C13 (PASSer), C14 (variant classification), C15 (statistical tests)
gaps.missing: The repository contains only four R scripts covering LOESS residuals, distance decay, DEFATTR generation and IC50 comparison. There is no DiMSum experiment-design/config file, no AlphaFold3 input JSON, no PyMOL/ChimeraX script, and no script implementing the score normalisation, the variant classification thresholds, or the statistical tests and figures. Ten of sixteen computational steps have no executable artifact.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the DiMSum fitness experiment design and run command, the AlphaFold3 input specification, the structural-analysis scripts, and the classification/statistics/figure code, so the full path from ENA reads to published figures is executable rather than described.

gaps.missing: No release, no tag and no commit hash is cited from the paper; the Code Availability statement points at the default branch only. The repository was last pushed 2026-05-11, after the 2025-10-20 preprint date, so the branch state a reader retrieves is not the state the paper describes.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release archived to Zenodo (or cite the commit SHA current at submission) and reference that immutable identifier in the Code Availability statement.

gaps.where: C1 DiMSum parameters; C3 concentration selection; C4 AlphaFold3 settings; C9 BLASTP; C15 Dunn's test
gaps.missing: DiMSum is given four non-default settings but not the full experiment design (barcode/constant-region definitions, cutadapt trimming, replicate structure). The three spectinomycin concentrations are chosen by a qualitative criterion ('optimal separation between synonymous and nonsense variants') with no stated numeric rule or resulting concentration values. AlphaFold3 seeds, model selection and template usage are unstated. BLASTP is run with no parameters given. The R package providing Dunn's test is not named.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the DiMSum experiment-design table and command line, state the selected concentration values and the numeric selection criterion, record AlphaFold3 seeds/settings, and name the packages behind each statistical test.

gaps.missing: The AlphaFold3-predicted TF-DBD:motif structures that every structural analysis depends on are not deposited. The Zenodo record supplies RData score objects only; the paper supplies no coordinate files, so distance, rSASA, contact and pocket results cannot be recomputed from the stated inputs.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the predicted structure coordinate files (and the PASSer pocket PDBs) alongside the Zenodo RData objects.

gaps.where: C6 DNAproDB, C9 BLASTP 'Blast 2 Sequences', C13 PASSer/FPocket
gaps.missing: Three analyses are performed via public web servers whose backend versions and reference databases change over time and are not recorded (no access date, no server version, no database release).
gaps.how_to_close: Record the server version and access date for each web-tool invocation, or replace the web invocations with locally versioned equivalents (fpocket, blast+ with a pinned database release).

gaps.where: W1-W5: mutagenic library design and cloning, B1H DNA-binding selection, spectinomycin abundance selection, sequencing library preparation and NovaSeq sequencing
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the analysis from ENA reads onward.
